newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index eases early, eye on Tye Soon.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index eases early, eye on Tye Soon.

text.p: Singapore shares eased early Monday on broad selling of index-linked stocks while activity was mostly concentrated on newly-listed Tye Soon.
Trade in the automotive parts distributor took the limelight, accounting for about half the volume and rising to a high of Singapore $0.55 against an IPO price of S$0.31.
The Straits Times Industrials Index fell 10.04 points at 2,050.46. Losers outpaced gainers at 125 against 31.
"Volume is so thin because people are a little concerned about tomorrow's export figures and what the Fed will do," a dealer with a local brokerage said.
A 139-point fall on Wall Street on Friday to 7,195 also hit sentiment, a reflection of expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise interest rates on Tuesday.
Expectations of flat Singapore April non-oil exports on top of Friday's gross domestic product growth of 3.8 percent in the first quarter, also dampened overall demand.
Leading losers was SIA foreign shares, dipping to Singapore $12.70, off 60 cents, and SIA at S$7.35, down 15 cents, after posting only slightly improved 1996/97 results on Friday.
UOB foreign drew active buying, rising to S$14.80, up 10 cents.
